summary: Frontend-only test of QuakeGuard Expo app on 390x844 viewport. Home screen and Alert screen render correctly with all required testIDs. External POST to https://safequake.onrender.com/api/status succeeds with HTTP 200 and correct payload shape ({deviceId, status:'safe', client_name, timestamp, location{lat,lng,accuracy,error}, battery{level,state}}). However, after 200 response the success toast (alert-success-toast) never appears and the auto-navigation back to home does not occur — user stays on the alert screen. Dismiss test could not be verified because success flow blocked us on the alert screen.

ui_bugs.issue: After successful POST (console log confirms 'response status: 200'), neither alert-success-toast becomes visible nor does router.replace('/') execute — user stays on alert-screen ~8s later. Root cause likely a rendering/state issue after setStatus('sent'); worth verifying setTimeout is not being cleared by an unmount or that the 'sent' branch renders the toast component correctly (successToast is only in DOM while status==='sent').

integration_issues.flow: I'm Safe → POST → Toast → Return home
integration_issues.issue: External POST returns 200 with correct payload but UI does not transition to 'sent' state visibly. The 'MARKED SAFE' button text / green success toast / auto-nav to '/' were all absent when checked 6s and 8.5s after click. No HTTP 400 seen.

issues: Metric labels/values render cleanly with no overlap. Pulsing red UI, LIVE ALERT timer, EARTHQUAKE DETECTED heading, dismiss link and green 'I'M SAFE' pill all display correctly.
Hero, SYSTEM ACTIVE banner, 4 tip cards (DROP/COVER/HOLD ON/AFTER), sticky TRIGGER TEST ALERT button all correct.

react_native_issues.issue: Non-blocking deprecation warnings on web only: 'shadow* style props are deprecated. Use boxShadow' and 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents'. Safe to ignore for MVP but worth cleaning up later (index.tsx stickyScrim uses pointerEvents prop; shadow* usage in styles).

action_items: Investigate why alert-success-toast is never visible and router.replace('/') is not navigating after a 200 response. Confirm status transitions (idle → sending → sent) actually update state — consider logging setStatus('sent') and verifying the setTimeout fires. Possibly the react-native-reanimated repeats or an unhandled exception in Haptics.notificationAsync on web is throwing after the fetch resolves and breaking the sent branch.
After fix, verify auto-nav to '/' works and success toast appears for at least ~1s before navigation.
Optional cleanup: replace deprecated shadow* style props with boxShadow and move pointerEvents to style.
critical_code_review_comments: alert.tsx: successful POST path does not await the toast render — setStatus('sent') followed by 1200ms setTimeout is fine in theory, but if any subsequent throw occurs (e.g., haptic error already awaited earlier is not the culprit), the sent branch will not render. Consider wrapping setTimeout callback in try/catch and using an effect on status==='sent' instead.
alert.tsx: no test hook to force geolocation on web — permission prompts vary by browser; consider a graceful timeout on Location.getCurrentPositionAsync (it can hang on web).
theme.ts: SAFE_ENDPOINT is hardcoded; not a bug for MVP but should ideally come from env for parity with other endpoints.
index.tsx line 146: <LinearGradient pointerEvents='none'> — React Native deprecates prop; move to style.pointerEvents.

success_rate.frontend: 80% (rendering & payload OK, post-success UI transition failing)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Use viewport 390x844. Grant geolocation via playwright context.grant_permissions + set_geolocation before navigation. External POST works (200) — focus reproduction on the post-success UI: watch for alert-success-toast and navigation back to '/'. Console log '[QuakeGuard] I\'m Safe → response status: 200' is emitted, so fetch resolves correctly.
rca_of_issue: Reproduction: 1) Load app 2) Grant geolocation 3) Tap trigger-alert-btn 4) On /alert tap im-safe-btn 5) Observe console 'response status: 200'. Expected: green alert-success-toast visible, then after ~1.2s router.replace('/') returns to home. Actual: no toast visible, no navigation ~8s later. Likely cause: the sent branch's setTimeout(router.replace,1200) may be running but router.replace on web preview inside expo-router sometimes needs router.replace('/') vs router.push. Alternatively, an intermediate state update (e.g., Haptics.notificationAsync failure on web) may throw and mask state transition. Suggest wrapping the whole handler in try/finally, calling setStatus('sent') even earlier (after fetch res.ok check) and using useEffect(()=>{ if(status==='sent'){ const t=setTimeout(...); return ()=>clearTimeout(t);} }) to guarantee navigation.
